name: Alpine meadow
notes: Subalpine-alpine herb meadows and grasslands just above treeline: Alps/Pyrenees mat-grass and fescue meadows, Rocky Mountain wildflower meadows, Tibetan/Himalayan Kobresia meadows. Grasses and sedges dominate with showy forbs.

associations.name: Mat-grass (Nardus) meadow
associations.where: gently sloping acid pastures on leached soil just above treeline, long snow cover
associations.source: Ellenberg 1988 Vegetation Ecology of Central Europe (Nardetalia); Braun-Blanquet 1948

associations.name: Alpenrose-dwarf juniper heath
associations.where: steep slopes and edges of the meadow near treeline where snow lies late, acid soil
associations.source: Ellenberg 1988 (Rhododendro-Vaccinietum); Ozenda 1985 La vegetation de la chaine alpine

associations.name: Subalpine wildflower meadow
associations.where: moist, deep-soil slopes and basins below the ridges, snowmelt-fed
associations.source: Billings 1988 Alpine vegetation (Barbour & Billings North American Terrestrial Vegetation); Komarkova 1979 Alpine vegetation of the Indian Peaks

associations.name: Kobresia sedge meadow
associations.where: wide flat plateaus and rolling slopes of the Tibetan/Himalayan high plateau, cold and dry
associations.source: Miehe et al. 2019 The Kobresia pygmaea ecosystem of the Tibetan highlands (Science of the Total Environment); Chang 1981

associations.name: Edelweiss limestone grassland
